Facts found: Flick has no HTTP client (deny.toml: 'Flick ships no network code'); release binary is 4.5 MB against a 5 MB check:binary-size cap; ISC (ring) is not in the cargo-deny license allowlist. mlx-serve 26.9.1 is OpenAI-compatible: GET /v1/models lists id/state/capabilities/context_length; POST /v1/chat/completions with stream:true emits SSE 'data: {chat.completion.chunk}' lines with choices[0].delta.content (and reasoning deltas for reasoning models), a final usage chunk with choices:[] when stream_options.include_usage is set, then 'data: [DONE]'. It supports --log-file off, --log-level error, --prefix-cache-entries 0 (prefix-cache-disk is off by default), --tokenize-cache-entries, --model-dir, --max-resident-models, --idle-evict-secs, --api-key-env. sections.approach: New module `llm` (src/modules/llm/, id `llm`, table [llm]) that drives the platform chat Surface from flick-3cdd; it never imports the chat module. (1) Transport: spawn /usr/bin/curl per request from a named background thread (no new crate, zero binary-size cost, TLS to tailscale-serve https endpoints for free). Args carry only the URL and fixed flags (-q to ignore ~/.curlrc, -sS -N --no-progress-meter, --max-time, --data-binary @-); the JSON body goes over stdin, so prompt text never appears in argv/ps. Stdout SSE lines are parsed by a pure parser; deltas land in an Arc<Mutex<..>> inbox and the thread posts Event::ModuleChanged{module:"llm"} (rebuild/herdr pattern). Cancel = kill the child. The spawn is behind a fn-pointer hook so tests use a fake stream and the coverage floor holds. (2) Config: [[llm.servers]] {name, url, private=false}, default_server, default_model, system_prompt, history=true, max_tokens, timeout_secs, hotkey, private_hotkey. Model picker = view `models` filled from GET /v1/models of the chosen server (cached per server, refreshed on open). (3) Normal chat persists history in the module's own tables llm_threads/llm_messages (append-only migration, in flick.db; history=false disables; bounded to the newest N threads). Own tables because modules cannot share flick-3cdd's thread tables. (4) Private mode is a separate session type, not a flag on the normal path: PrivateSession holds the transcript in memory only, has no Serialize, a redacted Debug, and wipes its strings on clear/drop (best effort: overwrite bytes in place with safe code + black_box, also request/SSE buffers). It is only allowed to talk to servers with private=true (the new :11235 instance); with none configured it refuses with a clear message instead of falling back to :11234. It has no store access path, no CLI/control verb, no remote-agent read, no notifications, no feedback/activity hooks, and copy uses a new platform pasteboard writer that marks org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType+TransientType so Flick's own clipboard history skips it. The Surface is opened with a private flag: fixed window title, a persistent 'Private - nothing is saved' banner and distinct accent, sharingType none (excluded from screenshots/screen recording incl. Flick capture), spell-check/autocorrect/text-completion/state-restoration off. It clears on window close, Event::Locked, Event::Sleep, config reload, and quit. (5) Server side: a second LaunchDaemon com.jaymin.mlx-serve-private on 127.0.0.1:11235 with --log-file off --log-level error --prefix-cache-entries 0 --tokenize-cache-entries 0, no --prefix-cache-disk, no --lan-share, --max-resident-models 1 --idle-evict-secs 900 (only holds a model while used), StandardOut/ErrorPath /dev/null, Core limit 0; exposed tailnet-only with `tailscale serve --bg --https=11235 http://127.0.0.1:11235`. The repo ships the plist + install doc; the user applies them by hand. (6) A canary verification script proves no prompt text lands on disk on either machine.

sections.context: The user wants Wispr Flow-style dictation on the laptop (M4 Pro): hold right_cmd+right_shift, speak, release, and the transcript appears in the focused text field of any app. Hard constraint: audio and text never leave the laptop (no cloud STT, no KOTA, no peers). This is separate from the KOTA push-to-talk chord (right_cmd+right_alt -> kota-voice :8600). Flick already has the pieces around it: the `keys` module owns the one CGEventTap and emits chord edges (Event::Chord{index,down}) but only runs http/shell actions; `platform::ax::send_paste` and `platform::pasteboard` exist (clip module pastes this way); `platform::hud` shows the message card. Local environment checked: Homebrew whisper.cpp 1.9.4 ships whisper-cli, whisper-server, whisper-stream and parakeet-cli (Metal backend works on this M4 Pro); sox 14.4.2 with the coreaudio driver gives `rec`; ggml-base.bin and ggml-small.bin exist under ~/Library/Application Support/Screen Studio/models; no large-v3-turbo or ggml parakeet model is downloaded yet. Measured: whisper-cli cold process (load + Metal init + decode) on the 11 s jfk.wav takes 0.40 s with base and 0.61 s with small. The release binary is 4.5 MB against a 5.0 MB check:binary-size budget, so linking whisper.cpp (whisper-rs) is not an option. Seed flick-8e7c, epic flick-699e (section 5, independent of the other sections).
sections.approach:
New module `dictation` (src/modules/dictation/) that runs everything in-process except two subprocesses: the recorder and the STT engine.

1. Trigger: the keys module gets a new chord action kind `{ flick = "<module> <verb> [args]" }` that runs a Flick control request in-process. The keys worker thread calls a hook (plain fn pointer passed on keys' `modules!` line, the same pattern as `remote::Remote::new(control::net::HOOKS)`), which does `events::on_main(move || app::control(&words, Flags::default()))` and logs errors. It cannot call app::control directly, because Keys::on_event runs inside Registry::dispatch with the state borrowed. Config: `[[keys.chord]] name="dictate" keys=["right_cmd","right_shift"] on_down={flick="dictation start"} on_up={flick="dictation stop"}`. The chord stays in [[keys.chord]], not in [dictation]: modules never import each other and Event::Chord carries only an index (Event is Copy), so this keeps the tap in one place and needs no core change. The same action serves Cards' 'run a flick verb' later. One main-queue hop adds well under 1 ms.
2. Mic capture: spawn `/opt/homebrew/bin/rec -q -t raw -r 16000 -e signed -b 16 -c 1 -` (path configurable) on chord down. A reader thread keeps the PCM in memory, publishes an RMS level (Arc<AtomicU32>) for the HUD, and enforces max_seconds. Stop = SIGTERM, then drain. No temp file while recording. TCC attributes the mic access of the child to Flick.app (the responsible process). So Flick's Info.plist gets NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (scripts/bundle.sh). No hardened runtime, so no audio-input entitlement is needed. A platform fn reports and requests the AVCaptureDevice audio authorization for `flick dictation status`.
3. STT: run the engine subprocess on a worker thread with a time budget (pattern of src/modules/rebuild). Pure code writes a 16 kHz mono WAV into a 0700 dir (~/Library/Caches/Flick/dictation/, file 0600), then deletes it after the run, and wipes leftovers at Started. Engines: `whisper` (whisper-cli -m <model> -f <wav> -l <language> -nt -np [--prompt <prompt>]), the default; `parakeet` (parakeet-cli -m <model> -f <wav> -np); `command` (argv template with {wav} {model} {language}, transcript on stdout). The worker drops the transcript and posts ModuleChanged{module:"dictation"}; on_event drains it on the main thread. A pure cleanup step trims the text, removes whisper non-speech tokens ([BLANK_AUDIO], (music), and similar), drops the result when the clip RMS says silence (stops 'Thank you.' hallucinations), and optionally adds a trailing space.
4. Insertion (main thread, platform): wait (timer::after chain, no blocking) until the chord modifiers are up (keytap::current_flags, cap 500 ms). Then: if secure input is on, or the frontmost pid differs from the one at chord-up, do not insert; keep the text as `last` and show it in the HUD. Else default `insert = "paste"`: snapshot every pasteboard item and type, write the transcript with org.nspasteboard.TransientType + ConcealedType markers (clip history already skips those in pasteboard::copied_text), post cmd+V with explicit flags and the keytap injection mark (the keys engine ignores it, and held physical modifiers do not turn it into cmd+shift+V), then after restore_ms (default 250) restore the snapshot only if changeCount is still ours. `insert = "type"` posts CGEventKeyboardSetUnicodeString chunks for apps where paste misbehaves; it never touches the clipboard.
5. Feedback: a new small non-activating pill panel `platform::pill` (it does not touch platform::hud, which the Cards section (flick-7da1) reworks): Recording + level bar, Transcribing, Inserted/Error text, auto-hide. A self-rescheduling timer::after(0.05) refreshes the level only while recording, so an idle Flick has no timer. Esc cancels through a global key monitor installed only while the pill shows (pattern of platform::hud). A hold shorter than min_hold_ms (300) is discarded as an accidental press.
6. Privacy and safety: no network code in the module; transcripts and audio are never logged or stored (log lines carry durations and char counts only); `last` is memory only. `dictation` (every verb) is added to NET_DENIED, so a peer can never start the laptop mic. Verbs: `dictation start|stop|cancel|status|last`.

Latency target: from chord release to text in the field, at most 1.0 s for a 10 s utterance with whisper small/large-v3-turbo-q5_0, and at most 0.7 s with base/parakeet. If cold whisper-cli misses the target, a follow-up seed adds a warm `whisper-server` on 127.0.0.1 (engine `whisper-server`); it is not in this plan.

alternatives.name: Link whisper.cpp in-process (whisper-rs)
alternatives.rejected_because: The binary is 4.5/5.0 MB under check:binary-size, it adds a C++/Metal build to cargo and check:deps, and a crash in the engine would take Flick down. A subprocess costs about 0.2-0.4 s cold model load, which is within the latency target.

alternatives.name: Chord declared in [dictation] (dictation reads Event::Chord itself)
alternatives.rejected_because: Event::Chord has only the keys-internal index, Event is Copy (no name String), and dictation cannot ask keys which index is its chord (modules never import each other). A second CGEventTap in dictation would duplicate the keys machinery. The `{ flick = ... }` keys action is general and reusable.

alternatives.name: Keys action `{ shell = "flick dictation start" }` (no code change)
alternatives.rejected_because: works today, but it spawns a CLI process and makes a socket round trip per edge (about 10-30 ms). It also depends on the flick binary on the launchd PATH. Keep it as the documented fallback only.

alternatives.name: In-process mic via AVAudioEngine (objc2-avf-audio input tap + AVAudioConverter to 16 kHz)
alternatives.rejected_because: lower start latency and no sox dependency, but much more unsafe FFI (audio-thread block callbacks, format conversion) and a new crate. Revisit only if `rec` start latency clips first words (manual step measures it).

alternatives.name: whisper-stream (live streaming transcription)
alternatives.rejected_because: its sliding-window output is unstable and needs SDL2 capture. Push-to-talk on release does not need partial results.

alternatives.rejected_because: a Python env and cold interpreter start (1-2 s) on every call. whisper.cpp's parakeet-cli gives the same model family as a native binary, so it is offered as engine `parakeet` instead.

alternatives.rejected_because: no clipboard, but it fails silently in Electron/web views and terminals, and success cannot be verified reliably. Rejected as the default; paste is universal, and `type` covers the remaining cases.

steps.title: dictation module skeleton: [dictation] settings, pure session state machine, WAV/RMS/transcript-cleanup helpers, status verb, NET_DENIED entry
keys: `{ flick = "<module> <verb> ..." }` chord action that runs a local control request through a main-queue hook
platform: microphone authorization (status/request) + NSMicrophoneUsageDescription; pasteboard snapshot/restore + transient text; marked cmd+V with explicit flags and unicode typing
platform::pill: non-activating recording HUD (recording + level bar, transcribing, result/error) with Esc monitor while shown
dictation recorder + transcriber workers: `rec` raw-PCM reader thread with level and max length, engine subprocess (whisper/parakeet/command) with time budget, temp WAV lifecycle, Hooks for tests
dictation wiring: start/stop/cancel/last verbs, min hold, pill updates, modifier-release wait, focus and secure-input guards, paste/type insertion with clipboard restore
docs/dictation.md (setup, model download, keys chord, permissions, privacy, limits) + manual test checklist; ARCHITECTURE.md and help topic updates
Manual test pass on the laptop: run the dictation checklist, record latency per engine/model, file follow-ups (warm whisper-server, AVAudioEngine) if targets are missed

risks: Mic TCC for an ad-hoc signed accessory app: without NSMicrophoneUsageDescription in Flick's Info.plist, macOS kills or silences the `rec` child. An ad-hoc rebuild changes the cdhash and resets the grant, the same as for Accessibility, so prefer the Apple Development identity (bundle.sh already picks it). A denied mic gives all-zero PCM: status must say 'Microphone denied', not a blank transcript.
`rec` start latency (CoreAudio device open, about 50-150 ms) can clip the first syllable. The manual step measures this; the fallback is the AVAudioEngine follow-up.

Synthetic cmd+V while right_shift is still physically held can arrive as cmd+shift+V (Paste and Match Style, or other bindings). Mitigation: wait for the modifiers to come up, set explicit flags, and mark the event so the keys engine ignores it (an unmarked injected event also rewrites Engine.flags and can produce spurious chord edges).

Clipboard restore races: a slow app reads the pasteboard after the restore and pastes the old content, or the user copies during the window. Restore only if changeCount is unchanged since the transient write; restore_ms is configurable. Restoring re-adds the original text to clip history as newest (it dedupes), which matches the state before dictation.
Focus changes between release and insert, or the field is a password field: guarded by the frontmost-pid check and keytap::secure_input(). The text stays in `last` (memory only) and is not inserted.
Whisper hallucinates on silence or very short audio ('Thank you.', '[BLANK_AUDIO]'): min_hold_ms, an RMS silence gate and token cleanup. Optional: whisper-cli --vad with a silero VAD model path.
Chord overlap with KOTA push-to-talk: right_cmd is in both chords, and Engine.holds matches supersets. Pressing right_cmd+right_shift+right_alt fires both. Document this and test it manually.
A remote peer starting the mic: `dictation` must be in NET_DENIED (pinned in src/characterization/control_replies.rs); step 1 does this before any verb can record.

Gate traps from mulch: config.rs is at its 500-line budget (mx-3f01b5), so do not add DEFAULT_CONFIG tests there. Platform hook closures in mod.rs count against coverage (mx-16e3ab): keep real-platform fns in a Hooks struct and wire.rs. A pub platform fn first used in a later step needs cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason)) (mx-2d069e). Module tests must not use shared temp dirs (mx-231c5f). There is no main menu for edit keys, but Flick's own fields handle cmd+V (mx-43d850).

Model files are large (large-v3-turbo-q5_0 about 550 MB) and are not present. Flick never downloads them (no network). The docs give the exact curl/huggingface command, and status reports a missing model path clearly.
Latency: cold whisper-cli reloads the model on every call (small: 0.61 s for 11 s audio measured). large-v3-turbo may exceed 1 s; the follow-up is a warm whisper-server on loopback.
acceptance: Holding right_cmd+right_shift for 2-10 s while speaking and releasing inserts the transcript into the focused field of TextEdit, Safari (a web textarea), Slack/Electron, Terminal/Ghostty and Flick's own launcher field. Median release-to-text time is at most 1.0 s for a 10 s utterance with the configured default model, as measured in the manual step.

No network traffic during dictation: the dictation module contains no network code, engines are local binaries only, and `flick --host <laptop> dictation start` from a peer is refused with 'dictation start: not allowed over the network' (pinned in src/characterization/control_replies.rs).
The clipboard contents (text, image, or password-manager concealed item) are the same before and after a dictation, and the transcript never appears in `flick clip list`.
No temp audio file remains under ~/Library/Caches/Flick/dictation after a dictation, a cancel, an engine error or a timeout. Transcripts and audio never appear in Flick's logs or flick.db.
Esc while the pill shows cancels recording or transcription and inserts nothing. A hold shorter than min_hold_ms inserts nothing. Silence inserts nothing.
With secure input on, or after the frontmost app changed, nothing is pasted, the pill says why, and `flick dictation last` prints the transcript (local socket only).

`flick dictation status` reports engine, binary and model presence, microphone authorization (authorized/denied/not determined), the recorder binary and the current state. `flick keys list` shows the dictate chord with `flick dictation start/stop` actions.

config.example.toml documents every [dictation] key and the new keys `flick` action. ARCHITECTURE.md documents the keys flick action and its hook, platform::pill and the new platform fns. docs/dictation.md has setup, privacy, limits and the manual checklist.
scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step. The binary stays under scripts/binary-size-budget.json, and no budget file is loosened.

sections.approach:
One new module `sys` (src/modules/sys/, id "sys") owns everything: the per-machine verb, the fleet aggregation, the launcher view and the actions. One module avoids cross-module imports; it meets herdr only by pushing the `herdr/agents` view by name.

1. Metrics by shelling out to stock tools, not FFI and not new crates. One fixed probe script (const PROBE) prints sectioned output: `sysctl -n hw.ncpu hw.memsize kern.memorystatus_level vm.loadavg kern.boottime`, `df -kP / /System/Volumes/Data`, `pmset -g batt`, `pmset -g therm`. A pure parser (sys/probe.rs, 100% coverage floor) turns it into `Snapshot {host, cpu_load, ncpu, mem_total, mem_free_pct, disks, battery, thermal, uptime_secs, at}`. The same script and parser serve the local Flick (`/bin/sh -c PROBE`, 2 s budget) and the ssh fallback (`/usr/bin/ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <target> /bin/sh -s` with PROBE on stdin, 10 s budget), so the Mac Pro needs no Flick install. Rejected platform FFI (host_statistics64/IOKit): it adds unsafe code and a second, untestable code path while ssh still needs text parsing.

2. Service checks are local config `[[sys.service]]` (name, kind = http|tcp|launchd|process|command, target, optional warn/fail thresholds, `log` path, `restart = false`). Each machine checks its own services, so loopback services (kota-memory, life-ops) are checked by mbp-server's own Flick. http uses /usr/bin/curl -m 3 (no HTTP/TLS crate); tcp uses std TcpStream::connect_timeout; launchd parses `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` (state, pid, last exit); process uses pgrep -x; command (mailwatch backlog, docker ps, syncthing) runs an argv from local config only and compares a number to thresholds. Checks run on a worker thread, results cached with timestamps; the `sys snapshot` command answers from cache and starts a refresh (first call with an empty cache collects inline within the 2 s budget).

3. Aggregation on the laptop: `[[sys.machine]]` (name, via = local|flick|ssh, host for `flick --host`, ssh target, vnc URL, dash URL). via=flick asks the peer's Flick `sys snapshot --json` over the remote transport through a new client seam: `core::control::PeerHooks` (plain fn pointer, like NetHooks) implemented by src/cli/client.rs with connect 5 s / read 10 s budgets and passed on the modules! line. No subprocess per poll, and no module imports crate::cli. via=ssh runs PROBE plus the machine's laptop-configured http/tcp checks (from the laptop) and launchd/process checks (inside the same ssh call).

4. Cadence mirrors herdr io.rs: one round on a thread, one thread per machine with an epoch counter, Hooks for tests. Poll on LauncherOpened, view open and Wake; every 15 s while the fleet view is visible; optional `refresh_secs` (default 0, min 30) for background polling. Sleep stops the timer; Wake refreshes once. Idle Flick has no timers. Every row shows age; data older than 3x cadence shows as stale, unreachable machines keep their last snapshot greyed.

5. Network policy: `sys snapshot`, `sys services` and `sys fleet` are read-only and stay allowed over the network. `sys restart` and `sys tail` are added to NET_DENIED (run code / read files) and pinned in src/characterization/control_replies.rs. Restart and tail from the dashboard never go through a peer Flick: the laptop runs them locally or over ssh, for services that set `restart = true` / `log`, after a destructive Confirm whose rows show the exact command (`launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/<label>`, via ssh <target>).

6. UI: launcher ListView first (root item `sys:fleet` "Fleet", view `fleet` with one row per machine and one per service with status icon and metrics subtitle; view `machine` with detail and the log tail as view.text). The persistent window comes last, on the chat window Surface from flick-3cdd.

PeerHooks client seam: core::control::PeerHooks implemented by cli::client with time budgets (ARCHITECTURE.md)

risks: Main-thread stalls: child processes (sysctl, df, pmset, curl, launchctl, ssh) must never run on the main thread except the bounded first `sys snapshot`; follow the rebuild/herdr background-work rules and give every child a time budget with kill.

Network exposure: turning on mbp-server's listener lets the laptop read everything net_policy allows there (clipboard history, windows, tasks). Peers must name only the laptop; review NET_DENIED for every new sys verb (restart and tail denied).

Remote-code risk: restart and command checks run commands. Only local config defines them; restart needs restart = true plus a destructive Confirm showing the exact command; never accept a command from a peer reply or a card.

Config drift: config.toml is per machine (mbp-server copied peers = ["mbp-server"]); if dotfiles manage it, a shared file needs per-host overrides. Older Flick builds on peers answer `sys` with unknown command; show 'flick too old' and fall back to ssh when configured.

Parser brittleness: pmset/df/launchctl output differs across macOS versions (laptop 27.x vs Mac Pro 26.6) and on machines without battery; fixtures from both hosts, unknown fields degrade to absent, never to errors.
Sleep/wake: polls in flight across sleep return late; epoch counter must drop them (mx-82e6eb: late remote results re-created a removed machine).

Budgets: src/modules/<mod>.rs files near 500 lines (split views/actions/io like herdr); coverage floors for new pure files must be added, not lowered; closures on never-run lines cost llvm coverage (mx-9821ad); platform-hook closures in mod.rs count against floors (mx-16e3ab).
Tests must never ssh, curl a real host, run launchctl kickstart or touch real services: all I/O behind fn-pointer Hooks with fakes (as herdr testkit).
New module verbs fail with 'unknown command' from a stale ./target/debug/flick or installed app (mx-d434ed); manual checks need a rebuilt app on both laptop and mbp-server.
HTTPS check of kota-dash via ts.net cert depends on Tailscale serve; curl failure must be reported as the check's error text, not a crash.
acceptance: `flick sys snapshot` and `flick --json sys snapshot | jq .ok` on the laptop print cpu load, memory, disks, battery, uptime and thermal, answering in under 2 s; the probe parser has a 100% coverage floor in scripts/coverage-budgets.json.
`flick sys services` lists each configured [[sys.service]] with ok|warn|fail|unknown and a reason; on mbp-server kota-memory :8300 and life-ops :8700 show ok via its own Flick.

From the laptop, `flick --host mbp-server --json sys snapshot` answers once mbp-server has peers = [laptop name] and network access on; `flick --host mbp-server sys restart x` and `sys tail x` print 'not allowed over the network' (pinned in src/characterization/control_replies.rs).
`flick sys fleet` shows laptop (local), mbp-server (flick) and Mac Pro (ssh) with metrics and service states; an unreachable machine shows its error and last-known age without blocking the others.

Launcher: 'Fleet' root item opens a view with one row per machine and per service; Enter on a machine opens its detail; ⌘K offers Screen Sharing (vnc://), Open Dash, Tail Log and, only for restart = true services, Restart, which needs ⌘↵ on a confirm that shows the exact command.
An idle Flick (launcher closed, refresh_secs = 0) starts no sys child processes or timers over 60 s; with the fleet view open it polls every 15 s; after Sleep/Wake it refreshes once.
No new crates in Cargo.toml; target/release/flick stays under scripts/binary-size-budget.json; no unsafe outside src/platform; scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step.
